mi-oakland-2026-occ-morgan-alexandra.name: Alexandra Morgan
mi-oakland-2026-occ-morgan-alexandra.bio: VP of Talent Management at Finance of America and part-time Oakland University instructor; former Chief People Officer at Leader Dogs for the Blind.

positions.stance: Seeks accessible education that results in transferable skills and credentials leading to strong careers.
Advocates stronger employer partnerships, internships, career pathways, workforce credentials and programs responsive to emerging skill requirements.
Emphasizes responsible stewardship of college finances and trustee decisions.
Wants to make sure education keeps pace with the jobs employers are creating.

nj-essex-2026-commissioner-at-large-vict.name: Wynnie-Fred Victor Hinds
nj-essex-2026-commissioner-at-large-vict.bio: Executive Director of the Weequahic Park Association; former Co-Chair of the Newark Environmental Commission and former teacher.

positions.stance: "She fights for clean water as a human right."
Seeks to transform underutilized spaces "into engines of opportunity."
Pledges to ensure "that policy reflects community needs."

va-fairfax-2026-herndon-mayor-leblanc-ke.name: Keven J LeBlanc, Jr
va-fairfax-2026-herndon-mayor-leblanc-ke.bio: Executive and small business consultant and volunteer leader for Herndon community events.

va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-ezekilov.name: Josif N. Ezekilov
va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-ezekilov.bio: Activist and community organizer in Herndon supporting immigrant neighbors and affordable housing.

positions.stance: Supports maximizing affordable housing for those at or below 40% of area median income, including 100% affordable housing on town or faith-owned land.
Prioritize small and medium businesses over large corporations and make Herndon more walkable, especially along commercial areas.
Will push for a labor center offering apprenticeships, skills training, and summer jobs and internships for young people.
Supports immigrant neighbors by expanding access to legal representation and adopting policies to keep families together.
Expand public transportation connecting downtown Herndon with the Metro corridor, and create more bike lanes.
Plan of "opportunity for Herndon families, connecting Herndon residents with impactful resources, and ensuring Herndon has a voice for affordability."

va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-bruce-sa.name: Sabrina A. Bruce
va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-bruce-sa.bio: Twelve-year veteran of the U.S. Air Force and Space Force.

positions.stance: Supports more crosswalks in areas such as Elden Street and the Herndon Parkway where pedestrians make risky crossings.
Supports protected bike lanes and dedicated pedestrian pathways like the Sugarland Run Trail.
Commits to holding office hours and being available to the community to discuss town issues.
"I support ending Herndon's use of Flock cameras and any other similar technology."
Supports requiring developers near the Metro to set aside a percentage of new units for affordable housing.

va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-shafiq-y.name: Yasmin "Soniya" Shafiq
va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-shafiq-y.bio: Fairfax County government employee supporting the park system, SEIU member, and Fairfax County Election Officer.

positions.stance: Aims to increase affordable housing stock by mirroring Fairfax County policy in new developments around the Metro.
Wants to facilitate as much balanced zoning as possible while maintaining the town's growth.
Maintain and grow green, open and community spaces, including through developer negotiations and proffers.
Wants to explore ideas for judicious water usage and consult Public Works on recommendations.
Bring more walkability to the town and effectively connect Herndon to the Metro.

va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-yohannes.name: Meron T. Yohannes
va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-yohannes.bio: Vice Chair of the Herndon Planning Commission; former Senior Policy Advisor at the U.S. Department of Commerce and Bipartisan Policy Center policy analyst.

positions.stance: "Championing affordable and diverse housing options for every resident."
Transforming downtown and aging commercial areas into vibrant, mixed-use destinations.
"Closing equity gaps and building a greener, more connected Herndon where every voice is heard."
Developing the Metro area with density while keeping Herndon's small town feel.
Growing local businesses and the town's tax base.

va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-lloyd-mi.name: Michael T. Lloyd
va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-lloyd-mi.bio: Herndon Town Council member since 2024 with more than 40 years of financial planning experience.

va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-britt-ju.name: Justin K. Britt
va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-britt-ju.bio: Herndon small business owner and marketing director and project leader.

positions.stance: Bring accountability to long-vacant properties to grow the tax base and restore services like bulk trash pickup.
Wants clear, upfront development guidelines and transparent zoning toolkits aligned with the Small Area and Herndon 2050 plans.
Expedite permitting and tax abatements for those who renovate, while using a Vacant Property Registry and code enforcement against stagnant owners.
Prioritize getting the Comstock downtown development project back on track.
Once litigation is settled, turn empty spaces like the old Subaru dealership into temporary parks, community spaces or pop-up vendor hubs.

va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-reyes-al.name: Alexis "Alex" Reyes
va-fairfax-2026-herndon-council-reyes-al.bio: Teacher and former Army Reserves soldier; has served on the Herndon Town Council for almost two years.

positions.stance: Collaborate with Herndon police on strategies to address crime and encourage residents to join neighborhood watch programs.
Promises to improve communication between the Town Council and residents through transparency and engagement.
Committed to "reducing the tax rate; advocating for fiscal accountability; and streamlining governmental regulations."
Does not plan to seek an endorsement from any party.
"I look forward to never seeking business from Comstock for as long as I am an elected official."
Inform and engage the entire community to gather a wide range of opinions and ideas for the best possible solutions.
Attract destination businesses and events while respecting existing events such as Friday Night Live and WinterMarkt.
Work closely with town staff, recruit and retain the best people, and make it easier to do business with the town.
Manage town resources with transparency and accountability and keep the cost of living controlled, especially for older and less financially secure residents.
Ensure land use decisions do not change the community's nature in undesired ways or outpace infrastructure.

wa-pierce-2026-prosecutor-schnepf-coreen.name: Coreen Schnepf
wa-pierce-2026-prosecutor-schnepf-coreen.bio: Chief Criminal Deputy in the Pierce County Prosecutor's Office, with 20 years as a prosecutor in Pierce and Kitsap counties.

positions.stance: Focused on holding people who commit serious violence accountable, with cases built on strong evidence that hold up in court.
Will go after crimes that make daily life harder and more expensive, such as stolen cars and organized retail theft.
Wants the office to keep pace with technology, as evidence now includes body cam footage, GPS coordinates and cell phone records.
Pledges to "run the office free of politics," deciding on evidence and the law and showing what the office delivers for every dollar.

wa-pierce-2026-prosecutor-chushcoff-brya.name: Bryan Chushcoff
wa-pierce-2026-prosecutor-chushcoff-brya.bio: Pierce County Superior Court Judge for 28 years, including service as Presiding Judge.

positions.stance: Says effective management is essential to public safety and that performance data should drive strategy, accountability and course correction.
Cites a rise in bookings with no charges filed, from 8% in 2019 to 15.3% in 2024, as a management failure.
Says fewer felony filings alongside rising pending cases show the office is falling behind in resolving felony cases.
Says his decisions are "guided by facts, fairness, and accountability, not outside influence."
Will prioritize mentorship for new attorneys, advocate for increased funding to retain experienced staff, and reorganize the office to strengthen accountability.

wa-pierce-2026-auditor-farmer-linda.name: Linda Farmer
wa-pierce-2026-auditor-farmer-linda.bio: Pierce County Auditor since 2022; former Lakewood City Council member and Chief Communications Officer for the Washington State Department of Enterprise Services.

positions.stance: Focused on maintaining secure, fair and transparent elections while expanding access and education for voters.
Believes Auditor services should be easy to access, focusing on customer service, digital access and reducing barriers for residents.

wa-pierce-2026-auditor-townsend-damon.name: Damon Townsend
wa-pierce-2026-auditor-townsend-damon.bio: Former Pierce County Elections Supervisor (2014-2019) and network operations supervisor at Lightcurve.

positions.stance: Supports secure systems and auditable processes, judged by turnout, accuracy and audit performance, "not by partisan framing."
Wants shorter wait times for licensing, passports and recording, modern scheduling, and honest communication when something goes wrong.
Supports better digital workflows, reduced redundancy, responsible evaluation of emerging tools including AI, and resiliency planning.
Proposes live dashboards for licensing wait times, recording turnaround and elections performance, plus annual reporting "written for people."
Wants equal service across the county, better remote access to recording and licensing, and Auditor services traveling to remote communities.

wa-snohomish-2026-pud-comm1-logan-sid.name: Sid Logan
wa-snohomish-2026-pud-comm1-logan-sid.bio: Snohomish County PUD District 1 Commissioner since 2017; former engineer, transportation director and operations director.

positions.stance: Working to keep electric and water rates as low as possible while maintaining reliability and preparing for increased electricity demand.
"Strongly support" programs that help consumers lower bills and provide financial assistance to low-income seniors and families.
Supports customers who install solar panels or invest in the PUD's community solar project in Arlington.
Works to ensure the utility is ready for threats to low-cost hydro power, cyber attacks, and new renewable energy technologies.

wa-snohomish-2026-pud-comm1-stclair-jane.name: Janet St Clair
wa-snohomish-2026-pud-comm1-stclair-jane.bio: Island County Commissioner since 2018; former teacher, social worker and non-profit executive.

positions.stance: Protecting low rates and investing in affordable plans for small businesses, seniors and working families.
Investing in the energy grid and protecting infrastructure in the face of climate threats and cyber attacks.
Building a stronger voice for PUD customers through strategies that serve municipalities, tribes and rural communities.
Focusing on diversification, strategic capital planning and a balanced energy portfolio.
Supports planning for climate resiliency, flood mitigation and managing water pollutants to protect access to affordable, clean water.

co-adams-2026-assessor-zavala-glenna.name: Glenna Marie Zavala
co-adams-2026-assessor-zavala-glenna.bio: Has worked in the Adams County Assessor's Office for the past 10 years; previously worked in insurance and mortgage lending.

positions.stance: Will work to ensure residents are treated fairly while protecting taxpayer interests.
Will implement state valuation guidelines "in a responsible way."
"Saving Adams County taxpayers from inflated property taxes."
"Adams County property assessments that make sense."
Campaign theme is "No New Debt."
Does not believe in or advocate "the initiation of force as a means of achieving political or social goals."
Pledges to support the U.S. and Colorado constitutions and uphold the Centennial Home Rule Charter and its ordinances.
Will listen to the people of Colorado and work with anyone willing to have a dialog.
Seeks repeal of unwise laws, especially those "not worth the trouble and expense of enforcing on everyone."

co-jefferson-2026-assessor-ketcham-greg.name: Greg Ketcham
co-jefferson-2026-assessor-ketcham-greg.bio: Certified General Appraiser in the Jefferson County Assessor's Office.

positions.stance: Plans to examine the budget and provide technologies and systems that give employees ownership of office processes.
Plans to inspire staff to train others to assist across departments.
Aims to "upend the status quo" and create a more collaborative office experience.
Willing to "go to bat for both taxpayers and employees" of the Assessor's Office and examine rules and norms.

mn-ramsey-2026-sheriff-fletcher-bob.name: Bob Fletcher
mn-ramsey-2026-sheriff-fletcher-bob.bio: Ramsey County Sheriff since 2019 and from 1994 to 2011; former Saint Paul Police commander, Saint Paul City Council member and Vadnais Heights mayor.
